   MEMORANDUM

  Agenda Item #:  1
  Meeting Date: 06/08/16

TO:  CITY COUNCIL
  PLANNING COMMISSION

THRU:  ANTON DAHLERBRUCH, CITY MANAGER /s/

FROM:  SHERI REPP-LOADSMAN, DEPUTY CITY MANAGER
  PLANNING AND BUILDING DIRECTOR /s/

SUBJECT:  WIRELESS TELECOMMUNICATIONS FACILITIES (CELL SITING)
  APPLICATIONS: THE LAW, THE CITY’S PROCESSES AND
  AUTHORITY

DATE:  JUNE 8, 2016

BACKGROUND

The increasing number of wireless communications facilities has significant potential for
beneficial and detrimental impacts within Palos Verdes Estates. Wireless communications
facilities are a vital link in the local emergency response network and in the general
communications needs of residents, businesses, visitors and government. Structures associated
with wireless telecommunications facilities, including antennas, antenna towers and equipment
cabinets, can interfere with views, natural vegetation, quiet seclusion, scenic values and the semi-
rural quality of life. The cumulative effect of numerous facilities being developed by competing
communication services providers can create unnecessary visual impacts through the development
of separate facilities. As such, wireless telecommunications facilities are required to be sited and
designed to provide the least intrusive means necessary and to minimize adverse impacts on
communities, neighborhoods, vistas, and natural resources.

The City recognizes the need to consider wireless telecommunications facilities permit
applications are to ensure consistent evaluation and uniform application of standards which are in
compliance with the Telecommunications Act of 1996, which states that the City “…shall not
unreasonably discriminate among providers of functionally equivalent services…” Further, the
Act states “nothing in this Act shall limit or affect the authority of a State or local government or
instrumentality thereof over decisions regarding the placement, construction, and modification of
personal wireless facilities.”
 The federal government limits local land use authority through regulations intended to facilitate
the development and distribution of advanced technologies. In particular, cities cannot prohibit or
effectively prohibit wireless facilities, unreasonably discriminate against wireless service
providers, or regulate such facilities on the basis of radio frequency emissions to the extent those
emissions comply with federal standards. Listed below is a summary of existing federal or state
regulations:

  •  Telecommunications Act: The Federal Telecommunications Act, amended in 1996, states
  that local government shall not prohibit or have the effect of prohibiting the provision of
  personal wireless services and shall not regulate facilities on the basis of environmental
  effects of Radio Frequency (RF) emissions. The Federal Communications Commission
  (FCC) regulates RF emissions based on standards for maximum permissible exposure and
  specific absorption rates for humans.

  •  Middle Class Tax Relief and Job Creation Act of 2012: Section 6409(a) of the federal
  statute is a provision intended to streamline the WCF modification process. The provision
  states that municipalities "may not deny, and shall approve" any request to modify or
  collocate with an "existing wireless tower or base station" when the request will not
  "substantially change the physical dimensions of such tower or base station." The FCC
  recently defined key terms such as "substantial change", and as a result modifications to
  existing facilities, which include 20-foot height and width extensions, must be approved
  by local governments.

  •  PRB-1: This FCC regulation requires reasonable accommodation of amateur radio
  facilities on a basis of "minimum practicable regulations" for Non- Commercial Antennas
  which involves the placement, screening, or height of antennas due to health, safety, and
  aesthetic considerations. California Government Code §65850.3 also implements this
  limited federal preemption. In addition to federal law, California law encourages the use
  of collocation because it reduces impacts related to grading, vegetation and fire-clearance
  that would occur if the same facility was separately ground-mounted. State law also
  requires that collocated facilities be analyzed under CEQA. Some provisions of state law
  have been pre-empted by federal regulations.

Most recently, the Federal Communications Commission issued regulations that require cities to
approve some collocations at previously approved facilities and allow for alterations to existing
facilities if the alteration is not considered a “substantial change” pursuant to Section 6409(a) and
the FCC’s regulations at 47 C.F.R. § 1.40001. These new federal rules are not limited to traditional
telecommunications towers but apply to essentially any communications facility. In addition,
California adopted new legislation that further restricts the time in which cities have to review
proposed installations and collocations

The current Municipal Code on Wireless Service Facilities does not include procedures on how to
review wireless telecommunication projects that fall under Section 6409(a). As directed by City
Council, staff will be undertaking revisions to the ordinance to address these recent changes with
State and federal law. In the meantime, the City is processing applications in compliance with
applicable laws.

  2
 Past Workshops

In October 2014, the Planning Commission reviewed preliminary applications for 18 potential
wireless telecommunication facilities by Crown Castle. The applications reflected 18 different
locations and designs with each pole varying in height and the type of equipment. At that time,
concerns were raised regarding the color, height, and aesthetics of the potential wireless
telecommunication facilities. Of the 18 potential locations, Crown Castle installed 7 mock-ups
throughout the City for the Planning Commission to better understand the design of the wireless
facility and provide for a more detailed analysis.

On July 28, 2015, the Planning Commission and City Council conducted a workshop to discuss
the process for reviewing wireless telecommunication facility applications.

On May 17, 2016, the Planning Commission conducted a workshop that discussed the following:

  •  Overview of City process
  •  Discussion of State and Federal Regulations
  •  Examples from other jurisdictions
  •  A look back at the Sprint v. Palos Verdes Estates lawsuit
  •  Past and current wireless facilities applications

Subsequent to this last workshop, the City Council requested a joint workshop to allow
additional discussion.

Current Workshop

There has been significant discussion of the ability for the City to provide a meaningful process
that appropriately balances the needs and interests of the community and the wireless
telecommunication carriers. There is a recognition that California cities are preempted from
regulating various aspects of wireless communications facility siting by both state and federal law.
In particular, cities cannot prohibit or effectively prohibit wireless facilities, unreasonably
discriminate against wireless service providers or regulate such facilities on the basis of radio
frequency emissions to the extent those emissions comply with federal standards. As a means of
ensuring open communications with all stakeholders, the workshop will provide an opportunity to
openly discuss the following:

  •  Definition of time, place and manner
  •  Role of “gap in coverage” in the review process
  •  City’s ordinance relative to State and Federal law
  •  Master planning and creating a streamlined process for preferred locations and designs.
  •  Explanation of Shot Clock
  •  What is the application, notice, mock-up, and review process

Current Applications

On behalf of AT&T, Crown Castle has submitted applications for 22 new wireless
telecommunication facility locations and 1 application to modify an existing site. Over the last
 several months, the Planning Commission has reviewed 12 of the 22 new applications and 1
application to modify an existing site. To date, 11 of the new AT&T wireless telecommunications
sites and 1 modification to an existing site have been approved by the Planning Commission. One
of these applications, WT-125-15, located within the right-of-way on the corner of Cataluna Place
and Granvia Altamira was appealed and subsequently approved by the City Council on February
9, 2016.

Crown Castle recently submitted 2 new applications for Verizon. Staff and our consultant are
reviewing the applications and will provide a status letter to identify any potential deficiencies by
June 12, 2016. Crown Castle advises that one additional application will be submitted on behalf
of Verizon. They are unaware of any additional applications that will be submitted in the
foreseeable future. Crown Castle will provide information at the workshop related to their efforts
to find the least intrusive locations and to facilitate colocation.

The amount of time and resources needed to process the wireless telecommunication facility
applications presents a significant demand on staff and the Planning Commission. It is also
recognized that the community and applicants are active participants and commit similar time and
effort. The process will benefit by having better understanding of the regulatory environment,
processes and procedures. There will continue to be a strong focus on alternative site analysis to
demonstrate the selection of the best location to meet the objectives of both the City and all other
stakeholders.
